name: ANNEXA-I
fullName: Andexanet for Factor Xa Inhibitor-Associated Acute ICH
population: n=530, ≥18, NIHSS n/a, ≤15 h from last FXa dose, ≤6 h from ICH onset
teachingPoint: AHA/ASA 2022 lists andexanet as Class IIa for FXa-associated ICH; ANNEXA-I refines hemostatic-vs-thrombotic trade-off.

name: ANNEXA-4
fullName: Full Study Report of Andexanet Alfa for Bleeding Associated with Factor Xa Inhibitors
population: n=352, mean 77, NIHSS acute major bleeding, ≤18 h after factor Xa inhibitor dose
finding: Anti-Xa activity reduced 92% (apixaban and rivaroxaban); excellent/good hemostasis 82% (204/249)
teachingPoint: Established andexanet reverses anti-Xa activity with 82% good hemostasis, at a 10% 30-day thrombotic event rate.

name: Andexanet vs 4F-PCC meta-analysis
fullName: Efficacy and Safety of Andexanet Alfa Versus Four Factor Prothrombin Complex Concentrate for Emergent Reversal of Factor Xa Inhibitor Associated Intracranial Hemorrhage: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
population: n=2977, Not reported in aggregate across the 16 included studies, NIHSS Not reported, Emergent reversal on presentation, as defined by each source study; literature searched to 16 May 2024
finding: Mixed, and internally inconsistent. Haemostatic efficacy favoured andexanet (RR 1.10). Overall mortality was lower with andexanet (RR 0.67), yet 30-day mortality specifically DID NOT differ (RR 0.82). Thromboembolic events were MORE frequent with andexanet (RR 1.47).
teachingPoint: Teaches that no randomised trial has ever compared andexanet with 4F-PCC head to head, and that US practice reverted to 4F-PCC because andexanet was withdrawn from the US market in December 2025 — a regulatory and supply consequence, not a demonstration that 4F-PCC works better.
